items.title: Warren Buffett and Greg Abel Are Bullish on 4 Contrarian Stocks That All Pay Dividends
items.summary: With a mountain of cash finally moving off the sidelines, Berkshire Hathaway's latest 13-F reveals four surprising dividend-paying bets that suggest Warren Buffett and his successor Greg Abel see opportunity where most investors still see risk.

items.title: 3 Reasons LEN is Risky and 1 Stock to Buy Instead
items.summary: Lennar’s stock price has taken a beating over the past six months, shedding 25% of its value and falling to $82.98 per share. This was partly driven by its softer quarterly results and may have investors wondering how to approach the situation.

items.title: Why the Weak Housing Market Is a Threat to the Broader Economy
items.summary: Apollo’s Torsten Sløk said a weak housing market will contribute little to GDP and provide less buffer for stocks if AI spending slows down.

items.title: Why Lennar (LEN) Dipped More Than Broader Market Today
items.summary: Lennar (LEN) concluded the recent trading session at $84.11, signifying a -2.57% move from its prior day's close.

items.title: Did Greg Abel Get Berkshire Hathaway Caught In a Housing Trap?
items.summary: Greg Abel just steered Berkshire Hathaway into a massive housing bet right as the market sends some of its ugliest demand signals in years. Whether that timing reflects visionary patience or a costly miscalculation depends on what you think comes next.

items.title: Toll Brothers Grew Its Earnings Per Share Without Growing Earnings
items.summary: A luxury builder in a soft market has bought back enough stock to outrun three years of shrinking profits, and the question is what happens when land competes for the same cash.

items.title: Berkshire bets on housing market recovery under CEO Greg Abel
items.summary: Berkshire Hathaway closed its $6.8 billion Taylor Morrison deal and grew stakes in two more homebuilders, signaling confidence under CEO Greg Abel.

items.title: Berkshire Boosts Its Bet: This AI Hyperscaler Is Now a Top-3 Holding
items.summary: Berkshire Hathaway's Q2 filing shows an 83% boost in its Alphabet stake to $37.8 billion, added to Lennar, and cut Capital One, Nucor, Kroger, and Constellation Brands holdings.
